PMID:35638208.setting: Comparison of ten established national hip fracture registries with consensus via the Fragility Fracture Network (FFN) Hip Fracture Audit Special Interest Group
PMID:35638208.country: International (England, Wales and Northern Ireland; Scotland; Australia and New Zealand; Republic of Ireland; Germany; the Netherlands; Sweden; Norway; Denmark; Spain)

cycle1.result: 215 unique questions across ten registries; only 72 (34%) used in more than one audit and 32 (15%) by more than half. Only 21/32 (65.6%) of 2014 MCD fields used by the majority of audits; only three fields (anaesthetic grade, operation, date/time of surgery) used by all ten; only one registry used all 32 fields.

PMID:35638208.intervention: Revised MCD produced by consensus: 22-field Core 2022 MCD plus 12-field optional Extended 2022 MCD, refined after FFN Asia-Pacific (July 2021) and Global FFN Congress (September 2021) feedback.
PMID:35638208.other_findings: Online feedback: 204/224 respondents (94.1%) agreed with inclusion of the reviewed fields and 157/224 (70.0%) agreed with the core versus extended split.

PMID:41951221.setting: Ten UK NHS trusts, elective primary total hip and knee arthroplasty (prospective multicentre audit)
PMID:41951221.standard: National waste management guidance: infectious (orange) stream only for suspected infectious agents, otherwise offensive (tiger-stripe) and general streams; no numerical target stated

cycle1.result: 92 THAs and 130 TKAs; mean total waste 14.79 kg per THA and 13.61 kg per TKA; infectious waste the largest category (9.88 kg THA, 8.68 kg TKA). Only 5/10 trusts used an offensive waste stream and 8/10 used recycling; significant inter-hospital variation in all waste categories (p < 0.001).

PMID:41951221.other_findings: On multivariable regression, hospital site was the main predictor of waste; trusts using offensive waste eliminated nearly all infectious waste. Switching streams estimated to save about £1.38 per THA and £1.22 per TKA.

PMID:41809278.topic: Alcohol withdrawal screening in trauma patients
PMID:41809278.setting: Community level 1 trauma centre (Conemaugh Memorial Medical Center), adult trauma admissions

cycle1.result: 30 (4.5%) had AWS (AWS score ≥ 3). AUDIT-C ≥ 5 predicted AWS with 90.0% sensitivity, 96.2% specificity, PPV 52.9%, NPV 99.5%; AUC 0.989.

PMID:41809278.other_findings: 48 patients (7.3%) were suboptimally managed: 23/51 (45%) with AUDIT-C ≥ 5 were not placed on CIWA-Ar and 25/611 (4.1%) with AUDIT-C < 5 were placed on CIWA-Ar.

PMID:37340473.topic: Online information quality for calcaneal apophysitis
PMID:37340473.setting: Top 50 Google-ranked websites per country on children's heel pain (content analysis)
PMID:37340473.standard: Elements of the DISCERN tool and JAMA instrument; SMOG readability; alignment with systematic review and trial evidence

cycle1.result: 118 (79%) hosted by private health services; mean SMOG 9.3 (SD 4.5); 140 (93%) gave at least one treatment recommendation but only 11 (7%) had all treatment recommendations supported by evidence.

PMID:37340473.other_findings: Only 75 (50%) gave a publication date and 67 (45%) described the condition as benign or self-limiting; some sites advertised surgery, shock wave therapy and laser.

PMID:38288220.setting: Single-site pain management service, Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (retrospective cohort audit with telephone survey)

cycle1.result: 81 (93%) satisfied with SCS; pain improvement group significantly associated with satisfaction (p = 0.010), with all patients in the >50% group satisfied.

PMID:38288220.other_findings: Pain improvement group also associated with sleep (p < 0.001), fatigue (p = 0.001), QoL (p = 0.003) and opioid use (p = 0.010); 49% increased neuropathic pain medication.

PMID:42488269.setting: Morning trauma meeting, Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, major trauma centre (Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust)
PMID:42488269.standard: Locally developed 10-domain, 20-point presentation quality score; complete presentation defined a priori as score ≥ 16

cycle1.result: Mean score 11.6 ± 3.0/20; complete presentations 18/75 (24.0%); management plan documented 49/75 (65.3%); tasks allocated 28/75 (37.3%); median clarification prompts 2 (IQR 1-3).

PMID:42488269.intervention: One-page 10-domain structured presentation template expanded from an acronym in the electronic patient record, introduced with a five-minute briefing, laminated copies in the meeting room and inclusion in the junior doctor induction pack.

cycle2.result: Mean score 17.1 ± 2.1/20 (difference 5.5, 95% CI 4.7-6.3; p<0.001); complete presentations 61/75 (81.3%; p<0.001); management plan 72/75 (96.0%); tasks allocated 67/75 (89.3%); median clarification prompts 1 (IQR 0-1).

PMID:42488269.other_findings: Median presentation duration unchanged (2.7 to 2.5 minutes, p=0.18); neurovascular status improved from 34/75 (45.3%) to 66/75 (88.0%). Sustainability beyond the initial period was not assessed.

PMID:33826800.setting: Single emergency department digital X-ray room, busy metropolitan public hospital (Logan Hospital)
PMID:33826800.standard: No established reject rate guideline stated; ALARA principle

cycle1.result: Overall reject rate 10.3% (1,193/11,596) and multiple reject rate 1.3% (147). Highest multiple reject rates among frequent projections: horizontal beam knee 32/380 (8.4%) and horizontal beam hip 17/182 (9.3%).

PMID:33826800.other_findings: Top reasons for rejection were positioning (58.0%) and anatomy cut-off (18.3%); AP pelvis reject rate 22.5% and AP chest 18.1%. Authors recommend staff education and re-audit.

PMID:41005792.topic: Hand and wrist surgical referral compliance with Evidence-based Interventions guidance
PMID:41005792.setting: Single community musculoskeletal service, Greater Manchester
PMID:41005792.standard: 2018 Evidence-based Interventions programme and Greater Manchester local guidance for carpal tunnel release, Dupuytren's release, ganglion excision and trigger finger release; project target ≥85% (provider internal national target 95%)

cycle1.result: Referral compliance 70%, 15% below the provider's internal national average and 25% below its 95% internal target.

PMID:41005792.intervention: Four PDSA cycles over 14 weeks: education session and case discussions, digital folder with clinical referral flowchart, knowledge quiz with case discussions, repeat quiz and Q&A.

cycle2.result: Compliance 71% after PDSA 1, 85% after PDSA 2, 99% after PDSA 3 and 100% in PDSA 4; average compliance improved 16% against the audit, 1% above the 85% target.

PMID:41005792.other_findings: Clinician confidence improved by 15% and quiz scores by 12%; referrals to injection clinics rose 3.2%. Improvement reported as sustained 6 months after the project.

PMID:41416323.topic: INR sample rejection in hip fracture
PMID:41416323.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)
PMID:41416323.standard: Correct filling of 3.2% sodium citrate tubes to maintain 9:1 blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, with discard tube first when using butterfly sets; no numerical target stated

cycle1.result: 66/399 INR samples rejected (16.5%, 95% CI 13.2-20.5%); 62 (94%) for underfilling and 4 (6%) for haemolysis.

PMID:41416323.intervention: Education sessions for junior doctors, phlebotomists and nurses on discard-tube use with butterfly sets, routine stocking of short-tubing collection devices, and visual reminder prompts at sampling points.

cycle2.result: 29/261 rejected (11.1%, 95% CI 7.8-15.5%); absolute reduction 5.4 percentage points, relative ~33%, not significant (p ≈ 0.11); 27 (93%) underfilling, 2 (7%) haemolysis.

PMID:41416323.other_findings: Among anticoagulated patients rejection rose from 17.4% to 19.6%; underfilling remained the dominant cause.
